sasha: Heads up — observing a reproducible drop in seed_cache hit-rate after yesterday's combined attention-kernel + quant-profile merge. Seen across two clusters (eu-west-1, us-west-2). :frowning:

sasha: Quick numbers from canary traffic:
```
before (master@prev): seed_cache_hit_rate=0.63
after (master@merged):  seed_cache_hit_rate=0.48
delta: -15ppt effective hits -> +~12% token cost
```

sasha: Latency p50/p95 unaffected, but downstream token counts and billing go up. This looks like key construction differences, not eviction pressure.
deploy-bot: Deployed attn-kernel v3.2 + quant-profile v2.1 to canary pool at 2026-03-17T22:10:05Z (sha: abcd1234)

maria: Thanks — do we have a repro harness to run synthetic prompts against both kernels? If so we can bisect.

sasha: Yes, I replayed the same prompt set (150k requests) against both variants with identical ordering. Repro is deterministic on our repro runner.

lee: I pulled a flamegraph. CPU and GPU utilization look normal. The key/hash time is slightly higher but not enough to explain 15ppt. I suspect the canonicalization step changed ordering of optional metadata fields.

aj: Ran a diff on the key bytes from the kv-prefetcher. Here's a minimal /real example (hex truncated):
```
legacy_key:  1f8a..7b0a | prompt_seed_len=24|lang=en
merged_key:  1f8a..9c3d | prompt_len=24|lang=en|temperature=0.7
```
aj: The merged runtime started including defaulted sampling params (temperature/top_p) into the cache key for certain model adapters — previously those were excluded. That would blow up cache cardinality for many requests.

sasha: Nice catch. Any quick patch to drop defaulted params from keying while we figure out intended behavior?

nina: We can add a compatibility mode flag `seed_cache.key_mode=strip-defaults` at runtime. I'll push a config toggle to canary tomorrow morning. Also propose adding a unit test to assert identical key generation between legacy and new kernel for requests with default sampling params.

ops-bot: Canary rollout note: reducing canary traffic to 10% for attn-kernel v3.2 until mitigation applied.

maria: If we do that, let's also update routing policy so Dedicated customers keep using legacy for 24h. We want to avoid cost spike on paid tenants.

lee: Additional datapoint: the merged kernel also changed an ordering inside the small-struct serialization when a prompt has metadata map. Most clients send metadata in insertion order; the new serializer sorts keys by hash for "efficiency". That changes the serialized bytes and therefore keys.

aj: Proposed fix: canonicalize by explicit sorted key list only for fields that are semantically relevant (e.g., prompt text, model id, user id) and ignore other runtime ephemeral params. I'll open a PR with tests reproducing the misswave.

sasha: For immediate mitigation, can we enable a post-hoc normalize step in the cache lookup code: normalize_metadata(map)->drop-defaults & filter-only-permitted-keys. Low-risk and fast.

nina: I can land the normalize step behind a runtime flag. Timeline: PR today, internal canary tomorrow, rollout by EOD if green.

maria: Make sure we have an eval for sample quality — we shouldn't hide real changes to sampling semantics. If keys are normalized we could mask intended new behavior.

aj: Agree — feature toggle + telemetry. I'll emit an event when normalization changes key shape so Optimize can compare quality deltas on sample set.

sasha: Action items:
- aj: PR to strip default sampling params from key generation + unit tests (owner: aj) — due: today EOD
- nina: runtime flag seed_cache.key_mode and canary rollout (owner: nina) — due: tomorrow AM
- maria: route Dedicated to legacy kernel for 24h and notify sales (owner: maria) — due: now
- lee: add perf / flamegraph comparison to the PR (owner: lee) — due: PR review

lee: one more note — there's a weird interaction where quant-profile changed a padding alignment which altered the serialized model signature length by 8 bytes for long prompts; that could change key collisions in some hash windows. Worth including in tests.

ops-bot: Incident risk flagged: billing impact severity=medium. Pager not triggered. Creating tracking ticket INF-4627.

sasha: I'll follow up after the PR lands and we run a full 500k replay. If the normalization recovers hit-rate to ~0.62 and no quality regression we'll promote the change.

nina: Landing PR now to my branch. Will post canary diff once ready. :thumbsup:

aj: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infer/runtime/+/2345 — contains key diffs, test vectors, and sample telemetry hooks.

lee: reviewed and left comments. Two minor nits.

maria: routed Dedicated away from merged kernel. Sales notified.

sasha: Thanks everyone. Reopen thread if we see further regressions after canary bump.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-4627 updated: assignees=[aj,nina,lee]; status=investigating"
